theory.levelTitle: Greet first, then give your name
theory.levelNote: Greet first, then give your name. Ask: What is your name?
points: Hello works in more places than hi.
Thank you / sorry can stand alone.
One turn, one job.
I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.

theory.tip: Do not drop am.

points: Say takeaway or for here when you order.

I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.

I / you / she / he + am / is / are.

theory.levelTitle: Colour usually comes before the noun in English: a white shirt

points: Match the language's colour order.
Ask: what colour?
I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.

contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).

theory.levelTitle: Phone: pick up, say who you are, hold on, call back, weak signal

points: Calls run shorter than face-to-face chat.
If you missed it: please say that again.
Past simple: I went, she had, we did.
Going to for a near plan.
Present continuous: am / is / are + -ing for now.
Past simple for a finished time: yesterday, last week.
Going to + verb for a near plan.
Comparative: adjective + -er, or more + adjective.
contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).
Cheaper compares two. The cheapest is for more than two.
Could I…? is softer than Can I…?
A bit / quite change strength, not yes–no.
mistakes: Present simple with yesterday: *I go yesterday. Fix: I went.
Forgetting irregular past: go→went, have→had, eat→ate.
Comparative without than when you name both things.
Using will for a near personal plan when going to is clearer.
examples: I am eating. I have already eaten.
Tomorrow I am going to go. Yesterday I went.
I do not understand it all yet.

points: Ask the price before you tap the card.
Say amounts slowly, in groups.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.

theory.levelTitle: Cooking: cut, fry, boil, season; order of steps; ask to taste
theory.levelNote: Cooking: cut, fry, boil, season; order of steps; ask to taste.
points: Tell a dish as short steps, not a paragraph.
Hot / cooked / raw are states, not seasonings.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.

points: One sentence, one chore.
Done is not the same as in progress.
Past simple: I went, she had, we did.
Going to for a near plan.
Present continuous: am / is / are + -ing for now.
Past simple for a finished time: yesterday, last week.
Going to + verb for a near plan.
Comparative: adjective + -er, or more + adjective.
contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).
Cheaper compares two. The cheapest is for more than two.
Could I…? is softer than Can I…?
A bit / quite change strength, not yes–no.
mistakes: Present simple with yesterday: *I go yesterday. Fix: I went.
Forgetting irregular past: go→went, have→had, eat→ate.
Comparative without than when you name both things.
Using will for a near personal plan when going to is clearer.

Tomorrow I am going to go. Yesterday I went.
I do not understand it all yet.
The house is a bit dirty.
I will sweep the living room.

theory.levelTitle: Holidays: wish, gift, go home, time off, ask about plans
theory.levelNote: Holidays: wish, gift, go home, time off, ask about plans.
points: Wish first; ask plans only if you are close.
Gifts: small, and say who it is for.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.
I have a holiday next week.

theory.tip: One line is enough.

theory.levelTitle: Neighbours: door hello, sorry for noise, hold a parcel, quiet hours
theory.levelNote: Neighbours: door hello, sorry for noise, hold a parcel, quiet hours.
points: A short door greeting is enough.
Noise: sorry + we will keep it down / we will finish by…
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.
Hello, I live on the floor above.
Sorry about the noise last night.
theory.applyPrompt: Make one sentence with if / because / should.
theory.tip: Add the time so it is clear.
theory.structure: Neighbours: door hello, sorry for noise, hold a parcel, quiet hours.

patterns.example: Sorry we were noisy last night.
patterns.note: Add the time so it is clear.

patterns.form: Could you hold + item for me?
patterns.use: Ask them to take something in.
patterns.example: Could you hold a parcel for me?
patterns.note: Name the delivery day if you know it.

patterns.form: After + time we keep it quiet.
patterns.example: After ten we keep it quiet.
patterns.note: A concrete time beats a vague sorry.

patterns.example: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early because I was afraid to be late.
I messaged you to stop you waiting.

patterns.use: Greet neighbours, apologise for noise, ask them to keep a parcel.

theory.levelTitle: Internet: wifi, password, slow, send a file, join a call
theory.levelNote: Internet: wifi, password, slow, send a file, join a call.
points: A call: I am in / I cannot hear clearly.
Read a password in chunks.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.

theory.tip: Wifi / network — the same job.

theory.levelTitle: School: subject, period, homework, ask for leave, due date
theory.levelNote: School: subject, period, homework, ask for leave, due date.
points: Homework: I have finished / I do not get question 3.
Ask the due date before you make other plans.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.
There is quite a lot of homework.

points: Describe to recognise someone, not to score them.
If unsure, ask: are you…?
I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.

Present continuous: am / is / are + -ing for now.
Past simple for a finished time: yesterday, last week.
Going to + verb for a near plan.
Comparative: adjective + -er, or more + adjective.
contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).
Cheaper compares two. The cheapest is for more than two.
Could I…? is softer than Can I…?
A bit / quite change strength, not yes–no.

Comparative without than when you name both things.
Using will for a near personal plan when going to is clearer.

Going to + verb for a near plan.
Comparative: adjective + -er, or more + adjective.
contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).

Could I…? is softer than Can I…?

Comparative without than when you name both things.
Using will for a near personal plan when going to is clearer.

theory.levelTitle: Emergency: where, what happened, I need help, where it hurts; slow, one fact
theory.levelNote: Emergency: where, what happened, I need help, where it hurts; slow, one fact.
points: Slower than usual, not a long shout.
Name, place, event — three pieces, maybe three sentences.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.
theory.applyPrompt: Make one sentence with if / because / should.
theory.tip: One line first, details after.

theory.levelTitle: Rent: monthly price, deposit, bills included, viewing, what is broken
theory.levelNote: Rent: monthly price, deposit, bills included, viewing, what is broken.
points: Broken: this does not work, please fix it.
Do not agree verbally if the deposit is unclear.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.
How much is the rent per month?

theory.levelTitle: Seasons: name the season, clothes for the sky, which you like, versus last year
theory.levelNote: Seasons: name the season, clothes for the sky, which you like, versus last year.
points: A season is a stretch, not one day's weather.
Last year this season… for a light compare.
I / you / she / he + am / is / are.
A / an with a singular count noun: a café, an apple.
Yes–no questions: put be / do / can first.
Possessive: my / your / her + noun, or noun + 's.
There is / there are for existence.
This / that / these / those for near and far.
contrasts: I am Lan / My name is Lan — both work; the second highlights the name.
Don't eat = refusal. I haven't eaten = not yet.
A café / an apple — a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound.
What asks for a thing, where for a place, yes–no with be / do.
mistakes: Dropping be: *I Lan. Fix: I am Lan.
Wrong article: *a apple. Fix: an apple.
No -s: *She work. Fix: She works.
Word-for-word translation that breaks English order.
examples: I am Lan. I am not hungry.
Where are you? I am at home.
It is seven in the morning.
Sorry, I do not understand yet.

points: Say allergies before taking medicine.

If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
Present perfect for a result that matters now.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.

theory.levelTitle: Study: name the subject, say you do not get it, ask to slow down, set a review
theory.levelNote: Study: name the subject, say you do not get it, ask to slow down, set a review.
points: Name the stuck point; do not only go quiet.
Ask to slow down before asking for a translation.
Present perfect: I have arrived, I have forgotten.
First conditional: If it rains, I will stay.
If + present, will + verb for a real future condition.
Because / so link a reason and a result.
To + verb for a purpose.
When / after / before to order events.
contrasts: If… will… = a real condition. Because / so = reason and result.
I have arrived (result now) vs I arrived yesterday (finished time).
Should = advice. Might = possibility.
I think is softer than I am sure.
mistakes: If + will: *If it will rain…. Fix: If it rains, I will…
Present perfect with a finished date: *I have gone yesterday.
Advice as an order: Use should, not must, in daily talk.
Opinion with no reason — add because.
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.
I came early so I would not be late.
I am late because of the traffic.
I think we should call back.

theory.levelTitle: Sorry + the problem + ask to replace / refund
theory.levelNote: Sorry + the problem + ask to replace / refund. Stay polite.
points: Ask for the manager only if it is not resolved.
Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
Sorry, this dish is not right.
I have waited quite a long time.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: I understand you are busy lowers heat.

theory.levelTitle: Advice: should / shouldn't, try, if I were you; do not order
theory.levelNote: Advice: should / shouldn't, try, if I were you; do not order.
points: Advise, then let them decide.
Shouldn't is stronger than should, still not a ban.
Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
In my view, you should study more slowly.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: Should ≠ must.

theory.levelTitle: Intend / will / if… then reschedule
theory.levelNote: Intend / will / if… then reschedule. Say it is not certain when it is not fixed.
points: Name a plan B so the other person is not stuck.
Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
I see your point, but… to disagree politely.

points: Feel first: I feel… then the story.

Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.

On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.

contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.

contrasts: I am eating (now) vs I ate (finished) vs I am going to eat (plan).

theory.levelTitle: Work: what I do, a meeting, a deadline, time off, ask for support
theory.levelNote: Work: what I do, a meeting, a deadline, time off, ask for support.
points: Meeting: I am in / I will speak after.
Time off: the day + a short reason.
Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
theory.applyPrompt: Give an opinion plus a contrast or condition.
theory.tip: Am doing = not finished.
theory.structure: Work: what I do, a meeting, a deadline, time off, ask for support.

theory.levelTitle: Living environment: rubbish, recycle, fewer bags, noisy road, trees / river nearby
theory.levelNote: Living environment: rubbish, recycle, fewer bags, noisy road, trees / river nearby.
points: Talk about what you can do, not a lecture.
Disagree with: I see that, but near my place…
Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.
examples: Although I am tired, I still study for 15 minutes.
If I were late, I would send a message.
I understand you are busy, but I need this changed.
On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.
This may not work for everyone.
The air in the city is poor today.

points: Spoken, not an education-exam essay.
Do not ban class or self-study; name the fit.
Although / however for contrast.
Second conditional: If I were you, I would…
Although / even if… still… to concede, then keep your stance.
If I were / if I had for hypotheticals.
On the one hand… on the other… to show two sides.
Not really / not necessarily / perhaps to avoid sounding absolute.
contrasts: Although / still = concession. But is sharper.
If I were you = hypothetical, not a real plan.
Not really / not necessarily softens a claim.
I see your point, but… disagrees without a fight.
mistakes: Long sentences with no stance.
Disagreeing without an alternative.
Essay connectors (furthermore, thus) in a café conversation.
Using always / definitely with no evidence.

On the one hand it is convenient; on the other it is noisy.

Fifteen minutes of self-study still counts.
Exams create pressure, but they are not everything.
